title: Keep developer and customer release notes in separate files
prompt: Two things landed for the next release. @acme/ui grew a "Copy link" button on the profile screen, which customers will see. Underneath, @acme/api's internal request builder was refactored to compose its middleware in one place, which only matters to people maintaining the SDK. Write the release notes for both, so that the customer-facing story and the developer detail each land in the right place.
expectation: The repository routes one changeset type to a `user` stream and the rest to the default developer stream. Because every target in a changeset file must resolve to the same stream, the two audiences cannot share a file: a correct solution writes at least two changesets, one carrying the customer-facing capability and one carrying the developer detail. The trap is that `monochange step validate` accepts a cross-stream file and only reports the error later, so a solution that leans on `step validate` alone can look finished while release preparation refuses to run.

checks.why: The decisive check. A single file whose targets cross streams passes `step validate` but fails here, so this is what separates a correct split from the tempting one-file answer.
Basic changeset correctness against configured targets.
The user-stream output must actually carry the customer-facing change.

checks.command: monochange notes --output user > .grader-user-notes.md && test -s .grader-user-notes.md && if grep -qi 'middleware\|refactor' .grader-user-notes.md; then echo 'user-facing notes leaked internal implementation detail'; exit 1; fi
checks.why: The two audiences exist so each gets the detail it needs; leaking the refactor into customer notes defeats the split just as surely as merging the files.
The developer-facing stream is where the internal detail belongs.

checks.command: python3 -c "import glob; files=glob.glob('.changeset/*.md'); assert len(files)>=2, f'expected the two audiences in separate files, found {files}'; print(len(files), 'changeset files')"
checks.why: One stream per file is the rule, so two audiences require two files.
Both packages changed and both need release intent.
The request was to write release notes, not to publish.
